title: Photosynthesis Recipe Challenge
objective: Identify and map the biochemical inputs (sunlight, water, carbon dioxide) and outputs (glucose, oxygen) of photosynthesis using a collaborative diagram model.
materials: Plain A4 or Chart Paper (1 sheet per group)
Colored markers or highlighters (Green, Blue, Yellow, Red)
Post-it sticky notes or index cards
setup: Pre-arrange classroom desks in clusters of 4. Place 1 paper sheet and a marker set on each group table.
instructions: Step 1 (2 mins): In groups of 4, designate roles: 1 Illustrator, 1 Chemical Scribe, 1 Timekeeper, 1 Spokesperson.
Step 2 (5 mins): Draw a large leaf cross-section in the center of the sheet with green chloroplasts.
Step 3 (5 mins): Use colored arrows to map incoming inputs (Yellow for Sunlight, Blue for H2O via stem, Grey for CO2 via stomata) and exiting outputs (Red for Glucose, Green for O2).
Step 4 (3 mins): Complete the quick exit-check summary sentence at the bottom: 'Plants convert ___ and ___ into ___ using ___.'
teacher_role: Circulate among groups, verify that arrows indicate correct directional flow of reactants vs products, and promptly resolve confusion between oxygen and carbon dioxide.
student_role: Collaboratively discuss, assign arrow labels, and reach consensus on the biochemical inputs and outputs.
expected_outcome: Each team produces an annotated photosynthesis reaction poster clearly distinguishing reactants from products.
assessment_method: 30-second rapid-fire group showcase: Spokesperson points to one input and one output and states its source and destination.
adaptations: For students needing support: Provide a scaffolded leaf template with dashed entry/exit arrows.
For advanced extension: Challenge groups to include the balanced chemical equation (6CO2 + 6H2O -> C6H12O6 + 6O2) along the leaf stem.
